title: Quiche Lorraine
intro: Crisp shortcrust, smoky bacon and a soft, just-set egg and cream custard.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Roll the pastry (store-bought is fine) into a 24 cm tart tin, prick the base and chill it.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Meanwhile, fry the lardons in a dry pan until golden, then drain them on kitchen paper.
steps.label: Bacon

steps.t: Line the pastry with baking paper and dried beans and blind-bake 15 minutes; remove the beans and bake 5 minutes more.
steps.label: Blind bake

steps.t: Whisk eggs, cream, milk, nutmeg, pepper and just a little salt: the bacon is already salty.
Lower the oven to 180 °C. Scatter the bacon over the base, pour in the custard and bake until golden and barely set in the middle.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it rest before slicing so it firms up and cuts cleanly.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Add 80 g grated Gruyère to the base for the version most people make in France.
Brush the blind-baked shell with beaten egg and bake 2 more minutes: the base stays crisp.
Serve with a green salad dressed with wine vinegar to cut the richness.

title: Torta pasqualina
intro: Liguria's Easter pie: chard, ricotta and whole eggs hidden in the filling.

steps.t: Wash the chard and blanch it in salted water, then drain, let cool, squeeze out well and chop.
steps.label: Chard

steps.t: Toss it in a pan with the oil over medium heat to dry it out well.
steps.label: Pan

steps.t: In a bowl mix ricotta, Parmigiano, 2 eggs, marjoram, salt and pepper, then stir in the chard.
Heat the oven to 180 °C. Line a 26 cm tin with one pastry sheet (store-bought is fine), edges overhanging, and spoon in the filling.
Make 4 hollows in the filling with the back of a spoon and crack a whole egg into each. Season lightly.
Cover with the second sheet, roll the edges to seal, prick the top away from the eggs and brush with oil.
Bake until the top is deep golden.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it cool a little before cutting: it's best warm or at room temperature.
steps.label: Cool

tips.t: Half chard and half spinach, or a few sliced artichokes, are equally classic Ligurian versions.
Next day it's perfect cold for an Easter Monday picnic; it keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Eggplant parmigiana
intro: Fried eggplant, tomato sauce, mozzarella and Parmigiano layered: a southern summer.

steps.t: Slice the eggplants lengthwise 5 mm thick, layer them in a colander with coarse salt, weigh down and let them drain.
steps.label: Drain

steps.t: Rinse them quickly and pat them very dry with kitchen paper.
Heat the oil to 170 °C and fry a few slices at a time until golden on both sides. Drain on paper.
steps.label: Fry

oven.t: Brush the slices with a little oil, lay them on lined trays and bake at 220 °C for 20 minutes, turning halfway.

airfryer.t: Brush the slices with a little oil and air-fry in batches at 200 °C for 12 minutes, turning halfway.

steps.t: Thinly slice the mozzarella and let it drain. Heat the oven to 200 °C.
In a baking dish, layer sauce (store-bought is fine), eggplant, mozzarella, Parmigiano and basil. Finish with sauce and Parmigiano.
Bake until bubbling at the edges and golden on top.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it rest before serving so it sets and the flavours meld. It's even better warm than hot.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Let the mozzarella drain in the fridge for a few hours so the parmigiana doesn't turn watery.
It's even better the next day and freezes well once baked, in portions.

title: Moussaka
intro: Roasted eggplant and potatoes, a cinnamon-scented meat sauce and a golden béchamel top.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220 °C. Slice the eggplants 1 cm and the potatoes 5 mm thick, brush with oil, salt and roast on trays, turning halfway.
steps.label: Roast veg

steps.t: Meanwhile, soften the chopped onion in 1 tbsp oil, then add garlic and meat and brown until no longer pink.
steps.label: Meat

steps.t: Splash in the wine, then add tomatoes, cinnamon, oregano, bay and salt and simmer gently until thick.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Meanwhile, warm the béchamel (store-bought is fine), take it off the heat and beat in the yolks and half the cheese.
Lower the oven to 180 °C. In a 30×20 cm dish, layer potatoes, half the eggplant, all the meat sauce minus the bay, then the rest of the eggplant.
Cover with béchamel, sprinkle with the remaining cheese and bake until the top is a deep golden brown.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it rest at least half an hour before cutting; that's what makes the slices hold.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: A pinch of allspice or ground cloves alongside the cinnamon is the Greek touch.
Make it a day ahead if you like: reheat covered at 170 °C for 25 minutes.

title: Lentil shepherd's pie
intro: The British classic made vegan: lentils and mushrooms under golden mashed potato.

steps.t: In a saucepan, soften the chopped onion, carrots and celery in 2 tbsp oil over medium heat.
steps.label: Soften

steps.t: Add garlic and chopped mushrooms and cook until their liquid has gone and they start to colour.
steps.label: Mushrooms

steps.t: Stir in tomato paste and thyme, then the rinsed lentils and hot stock (store-bought or cube is fine). Cover and simmer until tender and thick.
steps.label: Lentils

steps.t: Meanwhile, boil the peeled potato chunks in salted water until tender, and heat the oven to 200 °C.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Drain the potatoes and mash with the remaining oil, hot soy milk, salt and pepper until creamy.
Stir the peas into the lentils, check the seasoning and tip into a 25×20 cm dish.
Spread the mash on top, rough it up with a fork and bake until the ridges are golden.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it rest for a few minutes before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: A teaspoon of mustard or soy sauce in the lentils adds depth (soy sauce contains gluten).
Use half sweet potato in the mash for a brighter colour and a sweeter top.

title: Neapolitan potato gattò
intro: Naples' potato bake: rich mash with salami, ham and melting provola under a crust.

steps.t: Put the whole unpeeled potatoes in cold salted water and boil until a fork slides in easily.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Meanwhile, dice ham, salami and provola. Heat the oven to 200 °C, butter a 24 cm dish and coat it with half the breadcrumbs.
Peel the potatoes while still hot and press them through a potato ricer into a bowl.
Beat in 40 g butter, milk, eggs, Parmigiano, salt and pepper to a soft, smooth mixture.
Spread half the mixture in the dish, scatter over the ham, salami and provola and cover with the rest, levelling it.
Sprinkle with the remaining breadcrumbs, dot with the rest of the butter and bake until a golden crust forms.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it rest before serving so it slices without falling apart.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Vegetarian version: skip the cured meats, add more provola and some peas or sautéed mushrooms.
Slice leftovers and crisp them in a non-stick pan: they form an irresistible crust.

title: Chicken bastilla
intro: Crisp pastry over spiced chicken, eggs and almonds, dusted with sugar and cinnamon.

steps.t: Put the chicken in a pot with the grated onions, 50 g butter, saffron, ginger, turmeric, 1 tsp cinnamon, herbs, salt, pepper and water. Cover.
steps.label: Chicken

pressure.t: In a pressure cooker with the same ingredients, cook 20 minutes at pressure, until the chicken falls off the bone.

steps.t: Meanwhile toast the almonds in the oven at 180 °C for 8 minutes, until golden, and let them cool.
steps.label: Almonds

steps.t: Chop them coarsely with the powdered sugar (keep back 2 tbsp), 1 tsp cinnamon and the orange blossom water.
Lift out the chicken, now tender, and shred it, discarding skin and bones.
Reduce the onion sauce uncovered, stirring, until almost dry.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Pour in the beaten eggs and stir over low heat until softly set, like scrambled eggs. Let cool slightly.
steps.label: Eggs

steps.t: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Butter a 28 cm pie dish and lay in 5 buttered filo sheets, overlapping and hanging over the edge.
Layer the eggs, chicken and almonds. Fold the overhang in, top with the last 3 buttered sheets and tuck the edges under.
Bake at 180 °C for 30 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Rest for 5 minutes, dust with the remaining sugar, add lines of cinnamon and serve hot.

tips.t: Real warqa from Moroccan shops, instead of filo, gives an even thinner, flakier crust.
Cook the egg and onion mix until dry: if it's wet, the base of the bastilla goes soggy.
Reheat leftovers at 160 °C for 15 minutes and the pastry crisps up again.

title: Pastitsio (Greek baked pasta)
intro: Pasta, cinnamon-scented meat sauce and a thick golden béchamel: Greece's Sunday bake.

steps.t: Sauté the chopped onion in the oil, then add the garlic and beef and brown well, breaking it up.
steps.label: Meat

steps.t: Deglaze with the wine, then add passata, paste, cinnamon, cloves, water, salt and pepper; simmer until thick.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Meanwhile cook the pasta in salted water 2 minutes less than the package says and drain.
steps.label: Pasta

steps.t: Toss the pasta with 1 beaten egg and a third of the cheese.
Stir 2 egg yolks and another third of the cheese into the warm béchamel (store-bought is fine).
In an oiled 20 x 28 cm dish layer half the pasta, the meat sauce without cinnamon and cloves, then the rest of the pasta.
Cover with the béchamel, sprinkle with the remaining cheese and bake at 180 °C until deep golden.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Let it rest before cutting so the slices hold their shape.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Grated kefalotyri from a Greek shop instead of pecorino gives it the true Athenian taste.
It slices even better the next day: reheat portions at 160 °C for 15 minutes.

title: Spanakopita (spinach and feta pie)
intro: Crisp filo pie filled with spinach, feta, dill and spring onions.

steps.t: Wash the spinach, wilt it in a wide pot with no extra water, then cool and squeeze it very dry.
steps.label: Spinach

steps.t: Slice the spring onions and soften them in 2 tbsp oil until tender.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Roughly chop the spinach and mix with the onions, chopped herbs, crumbled feta, eggs and pepper. Go easy on salt.
Oil a 25 x 30 cm dish and lay in half the filo sheets one at a time, brushing each with oil and letting them overhang.
Spread in the filling, fold the edges over and cover with the rest of the sheets, each brushed with oil.
Score the top into portions with a sharp knife and sprinkle with a few drops of water.
Bake at 180 °C until the pastry is deep golden and crisp.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Let it cool a little before cutting: serve warm or at room temperature.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Keep the filo you are not using under a damp tea towel: in the air it dries and cracks.
With frozen spinach: use 750 g, thawed and squeezed dry, and skip the first step.
Great cold the next day; to crisp it up again, reheat 10 minutes at 170 °C.
